result.label: Runbook
result.title: Runbook: ledger-db failover
result.author: Marcus Webb
result.text:
1. Confirm the primary is unhealthy from two independent monitors.
2. Pause the payout batch in payouts-service.
3. Promote the synchronous replica using the failover script.
4. Point ledger-service at the new primary and verify journal writes succeed.
5. Rebuild the old primary as a replica and resume payouts.

result.label: Runbook
result.title: Runbook: fraud-scoring latency
result.author: Arjun Mehta
result.text:
1. Open the fraud-scoring dashboard and check p99 latency and pod CPU.
2. If CPU is above 70%, scale the deployment up by 50% and wait five minutes.
3. Check the feature store database for slow queries and connection saturation.
4. If latency is still high, restart the pods one at a time.
5. If payments are being declined, ask payments-api on-call to enable the conservative fallback.

params.title: Runbook: fraud-scoring latency
params.steps:
1. Check for a recent deploy to risk-rules first: INC-2026-032 was caused by dep:risk-rules-v2.8.0 (RISK-412: lower RULES_CACHE_TTL 300s -> 5s so rule edits apply faster).
2. If risk-rules RULES_CACHE_TTL was changed, roll it back. What fixed INC-2026-032: Priya rolled back RULES_CACHE_TTL to 300s; config-service load recovered
3. Watch config-service CPU and request rate: risk-rules calls config-service at request time; the service catalog does not list this dependency. (fact:learned-risk-rules-config-service)
4. Open the fraud-scoring dashboard and check p99 latency and pod CPU.
5. If CPU is above 70%, scale the deployment up by 50% and wait five minutes.
6. Check the feature store database for slow queries and connection saturation.
7. If latency is still high, restart the pods one at a time.
8. If payments are being declined, ask payments-api on-call to enable the conservative fallback.
